newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower, pressured by weather.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower, pressured by weather.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on prospects for improved crop conditions in the U.S. Plains and in Europe, traders said.

Weather in the northern Plains looked set to remain mostly dry over the weekend, allowing spring wheat seeding to advance. Wheat values also weakened on news that rain fell across the hard red winter wheat belt, and amid forecasts for moisture this weekend and next week in French wheat growing regions.
MGE spring wheat settled 2-1/2 to 7-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down five cents at $4.36 a bushel. July lost 6-1/2 cents to close at $4.35.
New crop September spring wheat shed 7-3/4 cents to close at $4.31-1/2.

Traders noted fund- and commission-related selling, with Benson-Quinn shedding one million bushels each of the May and July contracts. Atwood-Peavey sold one million May and one million September bushels.
